transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess I’ve been having some trouble keeping track of things lately. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I’ve missed or nearly missed things I really shouldn’t—like heart follow-up appointments, forgetting to call the clinic back, or even showing up to a repair job without the right tools. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I figured I should probably ask someone about it, if that makes sense.
Do you often find it hard to focus or stay distracted, especially during tasks that require sustained mental effort?

Yeah… I suppose I do, though I don’t want to overstate it. Like, I can sit down at the bridge table, or at one of the Fix-It Friends planning meetings, really intending to pay attention. And then after a bit my mind just sort of… slips off somewhere else. Next thing I know, I’ve missed half of what was said. It’s not that I don’t care, you know? It just happens.
Have you experienced any periods where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy? If so, how long did those feelings last?

I don’t think so, not in any big way. I mean, I have my off days like anyone, especially when I’m frustrated with myself, but I wouldn’t say I’ve felt hopeless or stopped enjoying things for a stretch of time. At least, nothing that stands out to me like that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often feel restless or find yourself acting impulsively, like you can't sit still or you jump into things without thinking them through?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m bouncing off the walls or anything. But since I’ve had to slow down on my walks and little projects, sitting still can feel pretty uncomfortable. Like there’s a motor running inside me and I don’t really have a good place to put that energy. I try not to make a fuss about it, but yes, I guess restless is a fair word for it.
Have you noticed feeling unusually tired or lacking energy, even if you haven’t been doing anything particularly strenuous?

I don’t think so, no… not unusually tired, anyway. I mean, I’m 68, so I have slower days, sure, but I wouldn’t say I’m lacking energy for no reason. At least nothing that’s seemed out of the ordinary to me. Does that answer it okay?
Have you had trouble starting tasks or seeing them through to completion, even if they’re things you know you need to do or want to do?

A little, yes… though I don’t know if I’d call it not finishing exactly. More like I sit down meaning to really pay attention, like at the bridge table or during a Fix-It Friends planning meeting, and after a while my mind just kind of… slips away. Then I realize I missed half of what was said, which is embarrassing.

I try to catch up and not make it obvious, but yes, I suppose that can make it harder to stay with what I meant to do. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking about?
Have you found yourself getting more irritable or frustrated than usual, especially in situations where you're trying to focus or stay on task?

I’m not sure I’d say more irritable than usual, no. I mean, I get a little annoyed with myself if I lose my place or can’t quite keep on track, but I try not to take that out on anybody.

Maybe frustrated is the better word, but even then… it doesn’t feel extreme to me. Just kind of, “Come on, pay attention,” that sort of thing. Does that make sense?
Have you had any trouble remembering things that you would normally have no problem recalling, like familiar names, recent events, or where you placed everyday items?

Yes… that’s actually more of what brought me in, I suppose. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I’ve been forgetting things I really should be able to keep straight.

Like heart follow-up appointments, or that I was supposed to call the clinic back. And with my repair group, I’ll show up and realize I didn’t bring the right tools, even though I knew perfectly well what we were going to do. It’s embarrassing, honestly.

I don’t know if that’s the kind of remembering you mean, but yes, that’s been happening.
Do you find that you need to rely on reminders, lists, or other people to keep track of things you used to handle on your own without much trouble?

Yes… I suppose I do, more than I used to. I don’t like to make too much of it, but I’ve started needing little reminders for things I really should be able to keep straight myself.

The main ones are things like my heart follow-up appointments, or remembering to call the clinic back. And with the repair group, I’ve had times where I show up and realize I didn’t bring the right tools, even though I knew what the job was. So, yes… lists and reminders help. I’m a bit embarrassed to admit it, but that’s probably a fair way to put it.

Have you noticed any changes in your thinking, memory, or reasoning that have affected your ability to manage daily activities on your own, like handling finances, driving, or following a conversation?

I wouldn’t say it’s stopped me from managing things completely on my own… at least I don’t think so. But what brings me in is that I keep forgetting things I really shouldn’t.

Like the heart follow-up appointments, or that I was supposed to call the clinic back. And then with the repair jobs, I’ll know what we’re doing, but I’ll show up without the right tools. That’s the sort of thing that’s been bothering me. I’m not sure if that counts as affecting daily activities the way you mean, but it’s enough that I thought I should mention it.

Have you had any trouble with things like getting confused about time, where you are, or having a hard time figuring out how to do things you used to manage easily, like following a recipe or handling your bills?

No… I don’t think so, not in that way. I mean, I’m not getting lost or confused about where I am, and I don’t think I’ve had trouble understanding how to do ordinary things.

Bills and things like that… I haven’t noticed a big problem there. If anything, it’s more that I worry I’m not keeping track as well as I should, but not that I can’t figure things out. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you find it hard to organize tasks or activities, like planning out steps or keeping things in order, more so than you used to?

I’m not sure I’d say organizing is harder exactly. I mean, I’ve always had my own way of doing things, and I don’t think I’m unable to plan steps or keep things in order.

Maybe I take a little more care now, just to make sure I haven’t missed something, but I haven’t really noticed a big change there. If you mean whether I’m getting confused about how to organize something, then no, I don’t think so. Does that make sense?
When did you first start noticing these issues with your memory and attention? Were they sudden, or have they been gradually getting worse over time?

I think it’s been… maybe a little over a year now. About a year and a couple months, if I’m being honest.

It didn’t feel like it happened all at once. It was more gradual, after that cardiac scare when I had to cut back on the walking and the projects that used to keep me kind of settled. Since then it’s been causing more real trouble than I’d like to admit. Does that sound like the kind of timeline you’re asking for?

Looking back, have you had similar difficulties with focus, forgetfulness, or being easily distracted earlier in life—like when you were in school or working full-time—or is this something that’s mostly started recently as you’ve gotten older?

Well… I guess if I’m being fair, it’s not completely new. I don’t want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything, but in grade school I was kind of known as the one who couldn’t sit still.

I’d blurt out answers, talk when I wasn’t supposed to, and I remember notes getting sent home about me talking too much. So, some of that goes way back, I suppose. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you continued to experience these kinds of attention and focus issues throughout your life, or would you say they improved at some point and have now returned?

I’d say it was there when I was young, yes. Maybe I learned to cover it better as I got older, or people just stopped calling it out as much.

But even as a boy in grade school, I was definitely the kid who couldn’t stay in his seat, blurted out answers, and got notes sent home for talking too much. I don’t love admitting that, but that was me. Is that helpful?
Looking back, were you able to manage your attention and focus better during your teenage years and early adulthood, or did these issues continue to affect you in different ways as you got older?

I think I managed it better for a long stretch, or at least I found ways around it. I don’t want to overstate it.

But yes, it did still show up in different ways. Even now, I can sit down at the bridge table or at one of those Fix-It Friends planning meetings fully meaning to pay attention, and after a while my mind sort of… slides off. Then I realize I’ve missed half of what was said.

So I suppose it didn’t completely go away. I just maybe got better at looking like I was following along. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have these issues with attention and forgetfulness caused you noticeable problems in your social life, work, or other important areas of your life?

Well… yes, I suppose it has, though I hate to make it sound worse than it is.

At the senior center, I help with that repair group, and lately it’s gotten to where they can’t really count on me the way they used to. I’ll forget something or miss part of what we agreed on, and then I feel awful about it.

And my doctor’s office has had to call me more than once about missed heart follow-ups, which is embarrassing. I don’t mean to be careless. It just… slips past me sometimes. Is that the sort of problem you mean?
